title: Francis Pelsart (or Francisco Pelsert, as spelt by Flinders).
notes:
He sailed from the Texee in 1628, and was wrecked on Houtman's Abrolhos in 1629. His boat being at anchor in 25 fathoms, some of his men swam ashore. Persart made his way back to the Dutch settlement at Batavia, 2000 miles off, to obtain rescue of his people. In his absence of several months, about 60 of his men mutinied and murdered about 120 people on the  island where they were wrecked. On his return with a vessel to carry all away, he captured all these murderers and shot them. One of the most tragic stories of Australian exploration.



By Batavian artist.
